history.summary: A temple of the Marwari community in Muzaffarpur city (Sikandarpur, near Pandit Nehru Stadium) dedicated to Rani Sati Dadi Ji (Narayani Devi), the folk goddess of the Jhunjhunu (Rajasthan) tradition. Like other Rani Sati temples, it serves as a community religious centre hosting daily puja and family events. Founding date and patron are undocumented in any source found — flagged UNVERIFIED. Not to be confused with the Rani Sati Dadi temples in Lohardaga (seq 435) or Jhunjhunu, Rajasthan.

name: Shri Rani Sati Mandir
town_description: Muzaffarpur is a major city of north Bihar and the headquarters of Muzaffarpur district in the Tirhut division, famous across India for its Shahi litchis. Situated on the Burhi Gandak river, it is an important commercial hub and railway junction of the region. The city also has historical associations with Jubba Sahni and the freedom fighter Khudiram Bose, and hosts Bihar's only planetarium and the L. S. College campus.

travel.airport: Patna (Jay Prakash Narayan International Airport), ~75 km away (verify).
travel.road: Near Pandit Nehru Stadium, Sikandarpur, Muzaffarpur; easily reachable by city roads (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: October-February; festival days see larger crowds.
